note: The super events of owner decision K52 (25 October 2026). Every text is ZIN-proposed and follows the accepted voice (docs/specs/02_lore/09_voice_and_style.md) and the knowledge layers (docs/lore/references/knowledge_layers.md) at the moment the flag is set. Ids are stable: never reuse an id for another moment. The hook flag is the global flag the owning module sets at the moment; the builder calls the super event right after every place that sets it.

retired.why: The waking is never world news: the owner's journey event zin_eindil.10 tells it to the realm that holds the man, and the first super event is the naming (id 4), shown only to that realm and Lorien's.

audienceNote: Owner decision K61: a moment the whole world would hear of (great wars, the fall of great capitals, the death or crowning of the great kings, the endings) shows to every human player; any other moment shows only to the human players whose realm is involved, and where it fits the human players next to an involved realm get a minor report event instead. Each audience is a scripted trigger zin_se_audience_<name> in country scope (common/scripted_triggers/zin_super_events.txt). Neighbours are bordering realms (any_neighbor_country), so no radius is needed.

events.title: The Golden King Is Dead
desc: The bells of Parim rang through the night, and by morning the whole city knew that the Golden King was dead, and the cooks who had been making ready for the next feast were sent home with the meat still on the spits.

He leaves a treasury full of promissory notes, a court full of men who bought their offices from him, and no heir that every camp of the Concord will accept, so the dominions have called their riders home and locked their seals in their strong-rooms.
The heralds will cry the mourning for thirty days, and the realm will spend every one of them deciding who wears the crown next.
events.button: Ring the bells and count the seals.
events.quote: For as long as he reigned he sold the offices of the realm to any man with the price of them, and now that he is dead every one of those men has come up to the palace to tell us how dearly he loved him.
events.attribution: A clerk of the treasury of Parim
events.picture: The great bell-towers of Parim at night, every bell swinging, torches in the streets below and a black mourning banner being let down the front of the gilded palace; in the foreground a crowd of courtiers in rich gold-trimmed clothes stands on the palace steps in small whispering knots, one of them already holding a sealed letter. The Golden King himself is not shown, or only as an empty gilded throne seen through an open door. Painted, sombre and a little ironic, gold against black.

sound.mood: court mourning, solemn and stately with a hint of hollowness
sound.instruments: tolling bells with a slow funeral pavane or lament for wind band (sackbuts, shawms, cornetts) or for organ and low choir

events.owner: Afrit and the Council (modules/mech_afrit.mjs, zin_afrit.txt effects)
events.title: The Deliverer Takes the Crown
desc: In the great temple of Parim, before the seat-holders of the Concord and more pilgrims than the squares could hold, the crown of Aenor has been set on the head of [zin_loc_deliverer], and the crowd that came to the city to mourn a king stayed to cheer the god they believe him to be.

The faithful say that the Deliverer healed the sick on the temple steps that same afternoon, and the Houses of the First Light opened their granaries to every poor family in the city, so that Parim went to bed with full bellies for the first time in a long while.
The old dominions keep their counsel, and the envoys of foreign crowns have written home that they have never seen Parim so happy, nor so quiet.
events.button: Parim has a king again, of a kind.
events.quote: We have prayed for a deliverer since the Necromancer burned our grandfathers' fields, and if the gods have answered at last, I do not see why we should be ashamed to say thank you.
events.attribution: Abbot-Steward Lozan Heron, at the crowning
events.picture: The interior of the great temple of Parim filled with white and gold banners and a dense crowd of pilgrims; at the far end, high on the steps under a shaft of light, the Deliverer in his public form (the canon Aurevan design: serene, radiant, robed in white and gold) receives the crown of Aenor; priests in white, censers, flower petals in the air, faces in the crowd weeping with joy. Nothing in the picture hints that he is anything but what the faithful believe; no demonic sign. Painted, luminous and triumphant, with one or two plainly dressed envoys at the edge watching without cheering.

sound.mood: radiant public ceremony, joyful and a little too perfect
sound.instruments: festive choir with organ, or a processional for choir and brass (Renaissance or early Baroque polyphony)

events.title: The Heir of Aen
desc: In the hall of King Lorien, before the oldest lords of the Gala, the stranger who came out of the northern ice has been given back his name: he is Eindil, son of Ein, son of Aen, an heir of the first king of men by his own blood.
Lorien, who remembers Dardan, says that he knew the face before he heard the voice, and the Keepers of the Mirror say the water showed them the same thing.
Outside that hall nobody yet knows it, and the Gala, who are very good at keeping things, have not decided whom to tell.
events.button: Then the line of Aen is not ended.
events.quote: Men count their kings by the names on the rolls, but we counted the line of Aen by their faces, and I had not seen that face in my halls for a very long time.
events.attribution: Words the Gala give to King Lorien
events.picture: A sunlit elven hall of the Gala with tall white pillars and gold light: the ancient King Lorien (canon v3 B: withered and ancient, extremely bright yellow glowing eyes, golden and white robe) stands before the black-haired man from the ice and lays a hand on his shoulder; between them a Keeper holds a shallow bowl of still water in which a faint crowned reflection shows; elven lords watch in silence. The man (Eindil v4 D face, black hair, blue eyes faintly glowing) is still in plain travelling clothes, not yet in armour. Painted, reverent and warm.

sound.mood: recognition and an old line remembered, reverent and warm
sound.instruments: harp and voice, or a slow chant for small choir with a plucked string accompaniment

report.title: Talk from the Gala Court
report.desc: Merchants back from the Gala say the elves have taken a great interest in a stranger from the north who is lodged in their king's own hall with more honour than any guest of men in living memory, and that nobody outside the hall will say why.

events.owner: World tension (modules/world_tension.mjs, zin_world_tension.txt effects; news zin_world.20)
events.title: The War of the Last Crowns
desc: There has been no single declaration and no single enemy, but the chroniclers have stopped pretending that the wars breaking out across Aoaz are separate quarrels: the dark powers are on the march, the old grudges between the crowns of men have found their excuse, and every road from the Wall to the southern sea is full of levies going one way and townsfolk going the other.

In the taverns of Parim they have already found a name for it, the War of the Last Crowns, because, as the wine-sellers put it, there will be fewer crowns at the end of it than at the start, and they mean to sell to whoever is left.
events.quote: In this year the wars of the age ran together like rivers in a spring flood, so that a man who marched against one enemy at sowing found himself fighting three by harvest, and the annalist, who has tried to keep them apart, begs the reader's patience.
events.attribution: The Chronicle of Aoaz, Fourth Age
events.picture: A wide painted panorama of the Middle Lands at dusk seen from a hill: in the distance several separate fires and columns of smoke along the horizon, banners of different crowns moving along different roads, levies marching one way and carts of fleeing townsfolk the other; a beacon blazes on the hill in the foreground with its keeper looking out. No single enemy is shown. Painted, sweeping and sombre, the light of evening.

sound.mood: the gathering of many hosts, grave and driving
sound.instruments: martial early music: drums, trumpets or sackbuts and shawms, an estampie or battle piece (for example a Renaissance battaglia) in a grave tempo

events.title: The Western Crossing
desc: The war-fleets of the West have put out across the central sea, every keel the Ford Council could buy, borrow or build, and the first of them have already run up on the beaches of the Middle Lands with their hosts behind them.

The western clans have come for an old debt, the one they say the kings in Parim have owed them since the truce of the Grey Ford, and their captains say openly that they mean to collect it in the capital itself.
On the shores of the Concord the beacons are burning, and the fishermen who saw the sails at dawn say there were too many of them to count before the light failed.
events.quote: My grandfather swore at the Grey Ford that we would have the debt back with interest, and he made us all swear it again over his grave, so you will understand that I have no choice in the matter but to get into this boat.
events.attribution: A clansman of Gunwyn, at the embarkation
events.picture: Dawn over the central sea: a great fleet of western longships and broad-sailed cogs with clan banners runs onto a pebbled beach, warriors in mail and fur jumping into the surf with shields and axes, more sails crowding the horizon behind them; on the headland above, a beacon has just been lit by a startled watchman of the Concord. Painted, energetic, cold sea light.

sound.mood: a sea-crossing war host, rhythmic and determined
sound.instruments: rowing rhythm on drums with low male voices singing a work song or march, or a drum-and-horn piece in a folk or early-music recording

events.title: The Black North Marches
desc: From the black shore of Zol's Mistake the dead have come out in their thousands, marching in better order than most living hosts have ever managed, along the frozen coasts and over the northern passes towards the lands of men.

The priests of every faith agree on very little, but they agree that this is the work of the Old God of Death whose name the black north bears, and in the villages nearest the Mistake the people have begun burning their own dead so that nothing they loved can be made to march.
The courts that once laughed at the fishermen's tales of black ships are sending for their harbour-masters to hear those tales again.
events.button: Burn the dead and bar the doors.
events.quote: We buried my father in the field behind the house with his boots on, because he always said he would sooner walk to the next life than be carried there, and this morning I am afraid he has taken us at our word.
events.attribution: A cottager of the Cold Lands
events.picture: A grey northern coast under a black sky: long ordered columns of the walking dead (skeletal, armoured skeletons in rusted mail and helms, K57) march along the shore and up into a mountain pass, ragged black banners without device among them; in the foreground a village on a ridge where folk are building a pyre and a woman holds back a child to watch. Zol himself does not appear in any form. Painted, cold and dreadful but restrained, no gore.

sound.mood: relentless cold dread, a dirge that marches
sound.instruments: low male chant or a Dies irae-like plainchant with deep drum, or a slow funeral march for low strings or low brass

events.title: Volgan Marches North
desc: Mirolon has fallen, and the hosts of the Ember Lands have come up out of the storms behind it: grave-hosts and ogre clans, the beasts of the southern deeps, and at their head Volgan himself, the Great Spirit whom the spirits of an older age stripped of his strength and threw into the Void, crowned and marching north.
The wardens of Mirolon warned every court of Aoaz for years that he was arming, and every court thanked them, gave them supper and sent them home.
The few envoys of Mirolon who still live have stopped asking for help and ask only for fresh horses, so that they can carry the warning further north.
events.quote: He waited a whole age in the dark beyond the world, the old song of the wardens says, and he will not mind waiting a little longer at your gate while you finish arguing about who should hold it.
events.attribution: Song of the wardens of Mirolon
events.picture: The southern passes under a sky of dark storm cloud lit from below by ember-red light: an endless host of grave-warriors, ogres with great clubs and monstrous beasts pours north over a broken mountain gate of Mirolon; above them, larger than life and partly made of the storm, Volgan in his canon form (v4 B: a purple cloak filled with darkness in which only two glowing green eyes show, a crown floating above the darkness, green magic at the hem). Painted, epic and menacing, purple, green and ember against black.

sound.mood: an overwhelming dark march, heavy and inexorable
sound.instruments: heavy drums and low brass or a low choir; a dark orchestral march or a slow heavy processional in a licensed recording

events.owner: Afrit and the Council (modules/mech_afrit.mjs, zin_afrit.txt effects)
events.title: The Name of the Deliverer
desc: The man the temples worshipped as Aurevan the Deliverer has another name, and it is now being shouted in every market of the Middle Lands: he is Afrit, son of Ein, grandson of Aen, who has lived far longer than any man should, and the Royal Council that governed Aenor in the Golden King's name answered to him all along.
What else he is, the priests of the twelve and the confessors of his own temples cannot agree, and both sides have begun to argue the point with stones as well as sermons.
The Houses of the First Light still keep their granaries open, though fewer of the poor are willing to be seen at their doors.
events.quote: I kept his birth rolls for twenty years and never once asked who was keeping mine, which I suppose is exactly what the rolls were for.
events.attribution: Sefan Daldar, Warden of the Rolls
events.picture: A crowded market square of Parim in grey morning light: a torn white and gold banner of the Deliverer lies trampled on the cobbles, a crier on a cart reads from a sealed proclamation, townsfolk argue and point, a confessor in white is shouted at, and on a wall someone has scrawled a mark over a painted image of the radiant Deliverer, half of the painted face scraped away to show darkness beneath. No lettering. Painted, tense and dramatic.

sound.mood: unmasking, unease turning to anger
sound.instruments: a dissonant or minor-key choral piece, or strings with an unsettled ostinato, in a licensed recording

events.owner: Afrit and the Council (modules/mech_afrit.mjs, zin_afrit.txt effects)
events.title: A King in the East
desc: Afrit did not go into the wilderness, as his enemies hoped, but east, where the courts that owed his temples their councillors, their granaries and their debts have knelt to him one after another, and in the halls of the East he has been proclaimed king over them all.

The envoys of the kneeling courts call his realm the Dominion of the East and speak of him with the old reverence, as though nothing had been said in Parim, while the courts that did not kneel are counting the temples in their own towns and closing the doors of the Houses one by one.
The caravan roads still run, but the caravan masters have started paying two tolls on every road, one to the old lords and one to the new.
events.button: Let the East keep him, if it can.
events.quote: A caravan master in the East has always paid one king for the road and another for the well, so you will forgive us if a third, who calls himself a god, does not strike us as much of a change.
events.attribution: A caravan master of Noris
events.picture: A great hall of the East with carved stone pillars, hanging lamps and rich carpets: eastern kings and lords in many styles of dress kneel in rows before a raised throne where the Deliverer sits crowned, still in his radiant white and gold public form but with the light around him grown colder and a long shadow behind the throne that does not match his shape; caravan goods and tribute chests at the edges. Painted, opulent and uneasy.

sound.mood: an oriental court in grim splendour, ceremonial and uneasy
sound.instruments: ceremonial plucked and bowed strings, frame drum and reed (oud, kanun, ney, zurna or similar) in a licensed traditional or early-music recording

events.title: Western Banners over Parim
desc: Parim has fallen to the hosts of the Western Crossing, which fought their way up the vale from the shores of the Concord to the oldest city of men and now hang their clan banners from the walls where the gold of Aenor flew for an age.

The court of Aenor has gone to another seat with what it could carry, the temples are shut, and the western captains, who do not understand the language of the city's prayers, are learning to govern it from its own clerks.
Every court of Aoaz is now waiting to see whether the West came to rule Parim or only to punish it.
events.button: A debt collected, and a city to keep.
events.quote: We took the gate at dawn and the market by noon, and by evening my lads had learned that a man who conquers Parim must also feed it, which nobody mentioned at the Ford Council.
events.attribution: A western captain in Parim
events.picture: The walls and gilded gate of Parim at evening with smoke rising from a few streets behind: western clan banners being hung over the gold banners of Aenor, western warriors in mail and fur standing guard, a line of city clerks in dark robes with ledgers being led up to a weary western captain at a trestle table in the gateway; townsfolk watching from windows. Painted, aftermath rather than battle, smoky gold light.

sound.mood: a conquered capital, grave triumph mixed with loss
sound.instruments: slow drums and a lament on bagpipe, horns or low winds, or a victory march played slowly in a licensed folk or early-music recording

events.title: The Heir Returns
desc: Eindil has come back to the war, and he has not come back on foot: the heir of Aen flew south out of the Magical Forest on the back of a dragon of the elven roosts, and the hosts who saw him pass over the lines say that they heard the dragon before they saw it and the cheering before either.

His friends have raised their banners to him, and crowns that have no love for one another are sending their captains to the Host of Eindil because it is the one army in the Middle Lands that everyone else's enemies fear.
In Parim, the men who called him an impostor not so long ago have become very careful about what they call him now.
events.button: Then the heir has friends after all.
events.quote: I have counted the dragons over the roosts every morning for longer than your kingdoms have kept records, and I have never once seen one carry a man willingly, so you may take it from me that this one chose him.
events.attribution: Perlan, Warden of the Dragon Roosts
events.picture: A great dragon with wide wings flies low over a field of armed hosts in the Middle Lands, the hosts below raising spears and banners and cheering; on its back rides Eindil in his canon armour (light blue armour and helmet, black hair, blue eyes glowing slightly) holding a blue sword aloft; a forest edge and smoke of war in the distance, bright sky breaking through cloud. Painted, heroic and hopeful.

sound.mood: hope returning, soaring and heroic
sound.instruments: trumpets or horns with full choir, or a bright orchestral or early-Baroque fanfare and chorus in a licensed recording

events.title: Varner Falls
desc: Varner the wizard is dead. When the dead of the black north broke the southern front and the hosts of the living began to give way, the old wizard of the Magical Lands raised wards over them such as nobody living had ever seen, and held them up until there was nothing left of him to hold them with, and the living came off the field only because he stayed on it.

The elves of the Magical Forest have put out their lamps for him, and the wizards of men, Bastian among them, have said in public what they used to say only among themselves, that nobody else alive knew half of what he knew.
events.button: Put out the lamps for him.
events.quote: He told us once that a ward is only a promise made with your whole strength, and that the trick of it is to choose carefully what you promise, because you will be held to it.
events.attribution: As the elves of the Magical Forest remember Varner
events.picture: A battlefield at dusk: a great dome of pale blue light stands over a retreating host of the living while the walking dead break against its edge like a dark tide; at its centre the old wizard Varner (canon design A, an old man in a wizard's robe and hat with a staff) stands alone with both arms raised, his figure already fading into the light. Painted, tragic and luminous, cold blue against black.

sound.mood: elegy for a protector, sorrowful and luminous
sound.instruments: slow elegy for strings or viol consort, or a requiem movement for choir, in a licensed recording

events.title: The Body of Volgan Is Broken
desc: On the field where the hosts of the living at last stood against the Ember Lands, the body that Volgan wore when he came back out of the Void has been broken apart like a burnt log in the hand, and the Great Spirit has gone from the field.

His grave-hosts fell where they stood or fled south without orders, the great ones of his court are quarrelling over what is left of his dominion, and the wardens of Mirolon have gone back to their passes to see what remains of their homes.
What remains of Volgan himself, no priest or wizard will say for certain, and the old wardens, who have been right about him before, are not yet singing the songs of victory.
events.quote: When the spirits threw him out of the world the first time, the wardens' song says, the wardens of that age danced in the passes for a week, and it is because we remember the dancing that we will not dance this time.
events.attribution: Song of the wardens of Mirolon
events.picture: A scorched battlefield under breaking storm clouds: an empty crown lies in the ash beside a torn purple cloak from which green light is fading and wisps of darkness drift away, while grave-warriors around it collapse into bones; in the background the hosts of the living stand exhausted and silent, a few wardens of Mirolon in grey looking on without celebrating. Painted, solemn, purple and green fading to grey dawn.

sound.mood: a great darkness broken, solemn relief that does not trust itself
sound.instruments: a slow hymn or chorale for choir or brass, ending unresolved, in a licensed recording

events.title: The Grave-Wind
desc: Out of the host of the black north something has come onto the field that is not one of the walking dead, a Great Spirit so tall that the soldiers who saw it measure it against the banners, and wherever it passes the dead stand straighter and the living cannot get their breath.

The Leren sailors who watched it from their ships know it from the oldest of their winter tales, and they say its name only in a whisper: Kusven, the grave-wind, the most loyal servant of the Old God of Death.
The priests say that the Old God himself does not walk the world and never has, and in the camps tonight the soldiers are finding that a very small comfort.
events.quote: I have stood in the line against orcs, trolls and the walking dead, and I never minded any of them half so much as the moment that thing looked down our line and the dead on either side of it stopped moving, as if they were waiting to see what we would do.
events.attribution: A serjeant of the living on the northern field
events.picture: A battlefield in the north under a black sky: Kusven, a vast and plainly supernatural Great Spirit (the owner-chosen Kusven redesign A, K41), towers over the host of the black north, which stands straighter around him; the skeletal armoured dead (K57) in ranks at his feet; facing him across the field the banners and spears of the living, small against him, and a few Leren ships on a grey sea at the edge. No lettering, no figure of Zol. Painted, terrible and still, cold blue-grey and black.

sound.mood: the world holding its breath, terror and stillness
sound.instruments: low choir or bowed strings with sustained tension and a single great drum, or a dark sacred choral piece, in a licensed recording (music, not a drone)

events.owner: The Lands of the Sun (modules/mech_sun.mjs, zin_sun.txt effects)
events.title: King Lorien Falls
desc: King Lorien of the Gala, who remembered Dardan, rode out with the oldest lords of his people and the ancient spirits who still answered him to stand between the living and Kusven, and none of them came home.

The soldiers who were there say that the old king's light was the last thing they saw on the field before the grave-wind drew back, wounded but not destroyed, into the black north, and the Gala have not yet told the other elves how they mean to mourn a king who has reigned since the First Age.
In every forest of the elves the songs have stopped, because nobody alive among them can remember a world without him in it.
events.quote: We asked him once why he stayed at home when the rest of the world went to war, and he said that he had been to war, and was only keeping the door open for the rest of us when we came back tired.
events.attribution: A lord of the Gala, after the king's fall
events.picture: A field at the edge of the northern dark: the ancient King Lorien (canon v3 B, withered, extremely bright yellow glowing eyes, golden and white robe) on a white horse rides into a wall of darkness with a small company of shining elven lords and pale luminous spirits, his own golden light blazing like a sunrise against the black; soldiers of the living watch from behind. Painted, heroic and tragic, gold and white against black.

sound.mood: the passing of the oldest king, noble grief
sound.instruments: a lament for solo voice and harp, or a slow polyphonic elegy for choir, in a licensed recording

events.owner: Afrit and the Council (modules/mech_afrit.mjs, zin_afrit.txt effects: zin_afrit_die)
events.title: Afrit Is Dead
desc: Afrit, son of Ein, whom half of Aoaz worshipped as the Deliverer and the other half learned to fear, is dead, and the heralds who brought the news to the courts have been made to repeat it twice, because nobody quite believed it the first time.

His temples in the East have shut their doors, his councillors are slipping out of the courts that kept them, and the Houses of the First Light, which fed half the poor of the Middle Lands, no longer know whom they serve.
In the markets they are already arguing over whether a god can die, and the priests of the twelve, for once, are content to let them argue.
events.quote: In this year died Afrit, son of Ein, who was called the Deliverer, and the annalist, who served his Council for most of his life without knowing it, has nothing to add except that he is sorry.
events.attribution: The Annals of Parim
events.picture: The throne room of the palace of Parim after battle, shafts of dusty light through broken windows: the true form of Afrit (owner drawing, v3 C: a winged demon with a great nose) lies fallen at the foot of the throne, wings spread and broken, the light of three small broken artifacts fading on the floor around him; at the edge of the light stand the silhouettes of the heir and a ranger with a bow, not triumphant. Painted, grim and quiet.

sound.mood: the fall of a false light, grave and cathartic
sound.instruments: a solemn choral or orchestral piece that resolves, for example a Renaissance motet or a slow Baroque chorus, in a licensed recording

events.title: A King of Aen's Line
desc: In the great hall of Parim, before the captains of every crown that fought beside him, Eindil, son of Ein, son of Aen, has been crowned King of Aenor, and the Lost Cause that a vain old king founded for his own glory has ended the age as the league of the living.
The Middle Lands are in ruins, the dead of the war are not yet all buried, and the new king has asked the crowns that stood with him for nothing they did not offer freely.
The chroniclers have begun the last pages of the Fourth Age, and for once they find they have very little to complain about.
events.button: Long live the king of Aen's line.
events.quote: And so the heir of Aen came home to Parim at the end of the Fourth Age, and the annalist, who began this book under a king he did not admire, closes it under one he does.
events.attribution: The Chronicle of Aoaz, Fourth Age
events.picture: The great hall of Parim, scarred by war but hung with the banners of many allied crowns (men, elves, dwarves, giants): Eindil in his canon light blue armour, helmet held at his side, kneels as an old crown is set on his black hair; Alleria of Selen, captains, elven lords and a giant stand witness; light falls through high windows. Painted, solemn and hopeful, not gaudy.

sound.mood: a hard-won coronation, majestic and deeply moving
sound.instruments: coronation anthem for choir, organ and brass or trumpets, in a licensed recording

events.title: Children of Volgan
desc: In this telling of the age the Great Spirit of the Ember Lands rules a ruined world. His grave-hosts stand on the plains of the Middle Lands, his client crowns kneel in their own halls and rule in his name, and the beasts of the south walk the roads where the caravans used to run.
The wardens of Mirolon warned every court of Aoaz, and every court thanked them, gave them supper and sent them home, and there are very few of those courts left to be sorry.
events.quote: He never hated the kingdoms of men, the last song of the wardens says; he only waited for them to quarrel, and they never once kept him waiting long.
events.attribution: The last song of the wardens of Mirolon
events.picture: Parim under an ember-red storm sky, its gold banners replaced by tattered purple ones; grave-warriors stand guard at the gates, kneeling kings in their own crowns line a ruined avenue, and above the palace hangs Volgan's canon form (purple cloak full of darkness, glowing green eyes, a floating crown). Painted, bleak and final.

sound.mood: the end of an age in darkness, heavy and final
sound.instruments: a dark requiem or lament for choir and low orchestra, or a slow dirge with tolling bell, in a licensed recording

events.title: The Ashen Throne
desc: In this telling of the age Afrit, son of Ein, who was worshipped as the Deliverer, rules all Aoaz from the throne of Parim. His temples are full again, his councillors sit in every court that owes the Houses of the First Light a favour, and the few who still say aloud what he is are not often heard saying it twice.
The crowns that fought him have made their peace or gone into the hills, and the bells of Parim ring for him on every feast day, as they once rang for the king before him.
events.button: The bells ring for him now.
events.quote: We still keep the feast of the Deliverer in our village, because the steward counts who comes, and my mother says a candle costs less than a visit from the Houses.
events.attribution: A cottager of the Middle Lands
events.picture: The throne of Parim on a grey ashen dais, the hall dim and full of incense smoke: the Deliverer sits crowned in his radiant public form, but his shadow on the wall behind is the winged demon of his true form; rows of courtiers and priests bow, and the gold of the hall is dulled with ash. Painted, oppressive and quiet.

sound.mood: a false god's peace, solemn, beautiful and hollow
sound.instruments: slow sacred choral music with organ, beautiful but cold, in a licensed recording

events.title: The Golden Court Endures
desc: In this telling of the age the Golden Court still rules in Parim. Whatever the long war took from the rest of Aoaz, the Golden Court kept its gold: the feasts go on, the offices are still for sale, and the men who bought them sit at the high table louder than ever.
The chroniclers, who expected to write the end of a dynasty, have instead been asked to write a very long poem in its praise, and are being paid by the line.
events.quote: I have sold the same office in the customs house four times since the war began, and every buyer has thanked me for it, which tells you all you need to know about the state of the realm.
events.attribution: Lord Treasurer Halmor Infous
events.picture: A lavish feast in the gilded hall of Parim: long tables loaded with gold plate, courtiers in gold-trimmed finery laughing and toasting, musicians in a gallery, a clerk at a side table counting coins for a line of office-buyers; through the tall windows the distant smoke of a war-torn land. Painted, rich, satirical and warm.

sound.mood: an oblivious court feast, merry and gilded
sound.instruments: Renaissance court dance music (galliard, pavane, branle) for consort of recorders, viols, lute or loud band, in a licensed recording

events.title: A Western Crown in Parim
desc: In this telling of the age western banners still fly over Parim, and the old quarrel of the West and Aenor has ended the other way round. The clans that crossed the central sea for an old debt have stayed to collect it for good, and their captains govern the oldest city of men with the help of its own clerks, whose prayers they still cannot follow.
The Concord meets in exile, in whatever hall it can find, and talks of the day it will take the city back.
events.button: The debt is paid in full.
events.quote: My grandfather wanted the debt back with interest, and I have given him Parim, so I hope he is satisfied wherever he is, because I have run out of things to give him.
events.attribution: A western captain-general in Parim
events.picture: Parim at noon with western clan banners on every tower: a western chieftain-king sits on the old gilded throne in fur and mail with a plain iron crown, his clan captains around him, while the city's clerks in dark robes bring ledgers; outside the windows the domes and temples of the old city. Painted, proud and a little out of place.

sound.mood: a rough-handed victory, proud and rustic
sound.instruments: a folk victory march or song with drums, pipes or fiddles and voices, in a licensed recording

events.title: Master of the Strait
desc: In this telling of the age Lerendor is master of the Narrow Strait, and every ship that crosses between the North Lands and the Middle Lands lowers its sail at Sonargur and pays the Sovereign's dues. The great harbour chain is raised for any keel that pays and lowered for any that does not, and the counting-house of Sonargur keeps longer hours than the king.
The crowns of the south, who grumble at every toll in Aoaz, grumble at this one too, and pay it.
events.quote: We have kept the chain at Sonargur for longer than anyone has kept a record of it, and in all that time no captain has ever paid the dues without telling us they were robbery, nor sailed past without paying them.
events.attribution: The harbour-master of Sonargur
events.picture: The harbour of Sonargur in the cold north: a massive iron chain stretched across the narrow strait between two towers, a line of merchant ships waiting with lowered sails, Leren tollmen in sea-blue rowing out with ledgers, King Ferlin's banner on the towers and grey sea under a pale sky. Painted, crisp and prosperous.

sound.mood: a northern sea power at its height, proud and steady
sound.instruments: a northern folk or Renaissance march with drums, horns and fiddles, or a sea song with a steady beat, in a licensed recording

events.title: One King in the East
desc: In this telling of the age the East has one king of its own. The courts that quarrelled over every well and caravan road from the rift to the deep sand now answer to one crown, and the caravan masters pay one treasury instead of seven, which is the first thing about the new order that anyone in the East has been glad of.
The envoys of the High King are already on the roads west, asking the other crowns of Aoaz what they mean to do about it.
events.quote: In my father's day a caravan from the rift to the deep sand paid seven tolls and three bribes, and now it pays one toll and nobody can tell me where the bribes have gone, which worries me more than the king does.
events.attribution: A caravan master of Stabilo
events.picture: A desert caravan city at sunset: a long caravan of camels and wagons passes under a single great gate bearing a new royal standard (no lettering), tollmen at one booth, envoys in eastern dress riding out westwards; minarets of no real-world faith and wells and palms. Painted, golden and expansive.

sound.mood: a united East, stately and prosperous
sound.instruments: eastern court or caravan music with oud, kanun, ney and frame drums, in a licensed traditional recording

events.title: The Age Unfinished
desc: No crown has ended the Fourth Age. The wars have dragged on into feuds and truces and the great quarrels of the age into treaties nobody quite keeps, and the chroniclers, who had hoped to close their books, have left the last pages blank for someone else to write.
The common folk do not seem to mind very much: the harvest is in, most of the roads are open, and an unfinished age is still one in which a person may grow old.
events.quote: The annalist had hoped to close this book with a coronation or a ruin, and must close it instead with the price of barley, which has gone up again.
events.attribution: The Chronicle of Aoaz, Fourth Age
events.picture: A chronicler's study at evening: a great open chronicle on a lectern, its last pages blank, a quill laid down beside it, and through the window a quiet countryside with a harvest being brought in on carts and a distant column of smoke on the horizon. Painted, wistful and calm, warm lamplight.

sound.mood: an open ending, reflective and gentle
sound.instruments: a quiet piece for lute, harp or a small consort, or a gentle pastoral, in a licensed recording

events.beat: B34 (divergence: the realm annexed with the body intact)
events.owner: Volgan (modules/mech_volgan.mjs, zin_dominion.txt effects: zin_volgan_withdraws_south, with news zin_dominion.29); owner answer Q-74 (K59)
events.title: The Fall of Nafeher
desc: Nafeher has fallen and the Dominion of the Ember Lands is broken: its grave-hosts are scattered, its sworn realms have torn up their oaths and gone their own way, and the hosts of the living stand in the hall where Volgan held his court.

Nobody, though, saw Volgan fall. The last riders out of the south say that he went down into the storms with his crown on his head, and the captains who searched the ruins found his throne cold and empty, with no body before it and no sign of where he went.
The wardens of Mirolon have gone back to their passes, and they have told every court that will listen that a Great Spirit who came back out of the Void once may well come back out of the storms.
events.button: Keep a watch on the passes.
events.quote: The old songs said he would come back out of the Void, and he did, so you will forgive us if we keep a fire burning at the passes for as long as there is anyone left in Mirolon to tend it.
events.attribution: A warden of Mirolon
events.picture: The throne hall of Nafeher in the Ember Lands, half ruined, its roof torn open to a swirling purple and ember-red storm in which a faint green glint can just be made out; the great throne stands empty and cold, with no body and no crown before it; soldiers of the living with torches search the rubble and look up uneasily at the storm, and a grey-cloaked warden of Mirolon stands apart watching the sky. Painted, an uneasy victory, ember, purple and grey.

sound.mood: an uneasy victory that does not trust itself, the enemy gone but not ended
sound.instruments: a slow piece for low strings or a small choir that ends unresolved, or a dark folk lament with a drone instrument, in a licensed recording

events.owner: Yeldenne and Glo (modules/mech_yeldenne.mjs, zin_glo.txt effects; zin_glo.21); owner answer K60
events.title: The Hall of Horos
desc: The old lord of the castle above Yeldenne is dead. The townsfolk of that small grey town in Pertolor's land called him Horos, as their grandmothers' grandmothers did, for he was a Great Spirit who had kept the high hall since before the town had a name.

Those who climbed to the hall afterwards found only dust on the high seat, and the heir of Aen coming down the castle road with a blue sword at his side and a crystal of old and holy power in his keeping, which the townsfolk say gives off a light like a clear winter morning.
What passed between the old spirit and the heir in that hall, the heir has not said, and the townsfolk, who have lived under the castle all their lives, would rather not guess.
events.quote: My father carried peat up to the castle every winter of his life, and the old lord thanked him every time, very gravely, as if a sack of peat were a great gift, and I believe now that to him it was.
events.attribution: A peat-cutter of Yeldenne
events.picture: The high hall of the Castle of Yeldenne in the far north, cold blue light through tall windows over snow: on the great stone high seat only a drift of grey dust and the faint shape where someone sat; before it stands the heir of Aen (Eindil v4 D: light blue armour, black hair, blue eyes faintly glowing), a blue sword at his side and a softly glowing crystal held in his hand. Horos is not shown as a figure (K56: story only); his absence is the subject. Painted, hushed and holy, blue and silver.

sound.mood: the passing of an ancient guardian, hushed and holy
sound.instruments: a slow sacred piece for small choir or for viol consort and organ, in a licensed recording

report.title: Lights at Yeldenne
report.desc: Carters coming down from the far north say that something has happened at the old castle above Yeldenne: the lights in its high windows went out one night, and the townsfolk have gone about with long faces ever since and will not say why.

events.owner: Volgan (modules/mech_volgan.mjs, zin_dominion.txt effects; zin_dominion.11, .24); owner answer K60
events.title: The Passes of Mirolon Fall
desc: The passes of Mirolon have fallen. Out of the storms of the Ember Lands came grave-hosts, ogre clans and worse, and the wardens who had held the mountain roads against the south for longer than any kingdom of men has kept records were driven from their towers one by one.

The court of Mirolon has gone into exile with the few banners it could save, and its envoys, who spent years warning every crown of Aoaz that this day would come, are knocking at the same doors again to say that it has.

The envoys say that Volgan himself leads the southern hosts, though there are still courts that would rather not believe it, and the scouts who got out say the hosts are camped in the passes and show no sign of going home.
events.button: Give the envoys a seat by the fire.
events.quote: We held the high gate for nine days on half rations, and on the tenth the captain told us to go down the back road and tell the world, so here I am telling you, and I would be grateful if you listened faster than the last court did.
events.attribution: A warden of Mirolon, in exile
events.picture: High mountain passes under an ember-red storm sky: grey stone watchtowers of the wardens burning along a ridge, a long column of grey-cloaked wardens and refugees with their banners retreating down a narrow mountain road, and behind them, pouring through the broken gate, a host of grave-warriors and ogres. Painted, desperate and grim, grey and ember.

sound.mood: a mountain stronghold lost, lament and defiance
sound.instruments: a lament on pipes, horns or low winds over a slow drum, or a mournful folk song with voices, in a licensed recording

report.title: Smoke over the Passes
report.desc: Herders coming up from the south say that the watch-fires on the passes of Mirolon have gone out, and that the road down from the high gate is full of people carrying everything they own on their backs.

events.owner: The eastern kings (modules/mech_east.mjs, zin_east.txt effects; zin_east.41 to .43); owner answer K60
events.title: The East Crosses the Rift
desc: A host of the eastern crowns has crossed the great rift into the Magical Lands, the first army of men to march under the elves' trees with fire and axes in living memory, and the border-wardens of the forests have fallen back on the old roosts and the deep groves.

The courts of the East say they have come for timber, for the roads and for old wrongs, and the elves say nothing at all, which those who know them like least of all; the dragons of the roosts have been seen in the air by day.
In the West and the Middle Lands, crowns busy with their own wars have begun to ask how the eastern courts, who agree on nothing, came to agree on this.
events.button: The forests will not burn quietly.
events.quote: The men of the East have brought axes enough to fell a forest, which is generous of them, because it will take them a good many generations to learn which of our trees are only trees.
events.attribution: A warden of the Magical Forest
events.picture: The edge of a vast ancient forest at the lip of a great rift: an eastern host in many styles of dress and armour crosses a long timber bridge over the chasm with wagons and axes, while elven archers wait unseen in the tall trees and a dragon wheels high above in daylight. Painted, tense and sweeping, gold-green forest against dusty eastern colours.

sound.mood: an invasion of an old forest, tense and martial
sound.instruments: frame drums, horns and reeds of an eastern or early-music martial piece, in a licensed recording

report.title: Trouble across the Rift
report.desc: Traders back from the East say that the eastern crowns have taken an army over the great rift into the elves' forests, and that the caravans are waiting at the wells until they know who holds the roads.
report.button: Keep the caravans at the wells.

events.owner: Zol's Mistake and Volgan (events zin_mistake_war.txt; offered by zin_dominion.14); owner answer K60
events.title: The Black Compact
desc: The hosts of the Ember Lands and the dead of the black north, who spent the first years of the war fighting each other as readily as anyone else, have stopped, and scouts on both fronts tell the same story of southern grave-hosts and northern dead marching on the same roads and turning together towards the Host of Eindil.

Nobody has seen a treaty, and the priests say there could be none, since the dead keep no oaths; the wardens of Mirolon, who know Volgan better than anyone, say only that he has never minded what kind of ally he had, so long as it was pointed the right way.
Across Aoaz the crowns of the living have begun counting their friends again.
events.button: Then the living must stand together.
events.quote: The south lot and the north lot used to fight each other over the same graveyard while we cheered them on from the hill, and I want you to know that I miss those days very much.
events.attribution: A serjeant of the Host of Eindil
events.picture: A dark plain at dusk under a split sky, ember-red to the south and black to the north: a column of Volgan's grave-warriors and ogres meets a column of the skeletal armoured dead of the black north (K57), and the two merge into one host marching the same way; scouts of the living watch from a ridge in the foreground. No figure of Zol and no figure of Volgan. Painted, ominous and still.

sound.mood: two darknesses becoming one, ominous and heavy
sound.instruments: a dark march for low brass and drums, or a heavy choral piece in a minor key, in a licensed recording

events.owner: Eindil's journey (events zin_eindil.txt, zin_eindil.110; zin_afrit.61, .62); owner answer K60
events.title: The Cliff
desc: Afrit has come back out of the East with an army, and the heir of Aen, who went out to meet him, has not come back. The few who were near say that the two of them met on the heights, that the heir was struck down and thrown from the cliff, and that nobody has found him since.
Afrit's heralds are already riding to every court to say that the heir is dead and that the war of the living is over.
The Host of Eindil has not broken up, though it does not know what it is waiting for, and in the camps the old soldiers say they will believe the heir is dead when they have seen the body.
events.quote: I have heard the heir declared dead twice in this war already, and both times he turned up for supper, so you will excuse me if I keep his place at the fire a while longer.
events.attribution: A cook of the Host of Eindil
events.picture: A windswept clifftop at dusk above a misty gorge: a dented light blue helmet lies near the broken edge, and a tall winged dark figure (Afrit's true form, v3 C) turns away from the edge with his back to the viewer; storm clouds and the far banners of two armies below. No body is shown. Painted, shocking and grim, cold blue and black.

sound.mood: shock and grief with a held breath of hope
sound.instruments: a lament for strings or voice that ends on an open, unresolved chord, in a licensed recording

events.owner: Eindil's journey (zin_eindil_lost; news zin_eindil.140, then zin_ending.80); owner answer K60
events.title: Without the Heir
desc: In this telling of the age the heir of Aen does not come back. Whatever happened to him, and the soldiers of his Host tell it a dozen different ways, he is gone out of the war, and the league that gathered round him must decide whether it can stand without him.

His captains still hold the field and the dark has not gone home, so the crowns of the living have done what crowns do: they have sent their envoys to argue about who should lead, and their armies to keep fighting while the envoys argue.
events.quote: We followed him because he was the heir, and we kept following him because he was the kind of man you follow, and now I suppose we shall find out which of those two reasons was the real one.
events.attribution: A captain of the league of the living
events.picture: An empty command tent at grey dawn: a light blue cloak and a helmet laid on the camp table beside a map, captains of many crowns (men, elves, dwarves) standing around it in silence, banners outside hanging still in the windless air. Painted, quiet grief, grey and blue.

sound.mood: a leaderless league, noble grief and resolve
sound.instruments: a slow funeral march or elegy for brass or strings, in a licensed recording
